Prebuilts.name: BOXX APEXX
Prebuilts.note: Workstations tuned for CAD, often overclocked for the single-core speed Revit and Rhino want. Phone support and a long warranty.

Prebuilts.name: Puget Systems
Prebuilts.note: Custom workstations with published CAD and render benchmarks. They spec the build with you and support it after.

Prebuilts.name: BIMBOX
Prebuilts.note: PCs built and tuned for Revit and BIM, with help setting them up. Aimed at architecture firms.

Prebuilts.name: ASUS ExpertCenter PB64
Prebuilts.note: Up to 64 GB, drives two displays up to 6K. Mounts behind a monitor, and silent.

Prebuilts.name: ASUS ExpertCenter PN55
Prebuilts.note: The AMD mini, with a stronger integrated GPU for light 3D. Drives two displays up to 6K.

Prebuilts.name: ASUS NUC 15 Pro
Prebuilts.note: Compact, with Thunderbolt 4 and a good dock ecosystem. Drives four 4K displays.

Prebuilts.name: Lenovo ThinkCentre Tiny (M90q)
Prebuilts.note: Up to 64 GB. A reliable business mini. vPro adds no value if you're buying for yourself, so don't pay extra for it.

Prebuilts.name: Lenovo ThinkCentre Neo 50t
Prebuilts.note: 32 GB, with a full GPU slot. Add an RTX 4060 to drive a 3D viewport.

Prebuilts.name: Dell Tower Plus
Prebuilts.note: Up to an RTX 4060 Ti from the factory. The cheapest tower that ships with a dedicated GPU.

Prebuilts.name: HP ProDesk 4 Tower
Prebuilts.note: A plain corporate desktop: cheap, reliable, and everywhere. Fine for documents and 2D, not built for 3D.

Prebuilts.name: Dell Pro Max Tower T2
Prebuilts.note: Certified for pro software. Pro GPUs only, no GeForce.

Prebuilts.name: HP Z2 Tower G9 / G10
Prebuilts.note: Certified for pro software, and quiet. Pro GPUs only.

Prebuilts.name: Lenovo ThinkStation P3 Tower
Prebuilts.note: Up to 128 GB and pro GPUs. A high memory ceiling for large models.

Prebuilts.name: HP Omen 35L
Prebuilts.note: RTX 5070 Ti and 32 GB from the factory. Mainstream and widely stocked, with a standard layout that's easy to upgrade later.

Prebuilts.name: MSI MAG Infinite S3
Prebuilts.note: RTX 5070, 750W PSU, clean design. Less gamer aesthetic than most.

Prebuilts.name: CyberPowerPC Gamer Xtreme
Prebuilts.note: Configurable. Order it with an RTX 5070 Ti and 64 GB. The cheapest way into a powerful GPU.

Prebuilts.name: iBuyPower / NZXT BLD
Prebuilts.note: Custom config. Pick your CPU, GPU, and RAM. Tidy cable work and quiet builds.

PrebuiltTypeNotes.builder: Bespoke builders who spec, test, and support the machine, and walk you through the order. The best route for a small firm with no IT.
PrebuiltTypeNotes.mini: Silent and tiny, with no dedicated GPU. Good for documents, drafting, and light modeling, not visualization.
PrebuiltTypeNotes.office: A standard office tower. A few fit a low-power GPU, enough for drafting and modeling, but never a fast one.
PrebuiltTypeNotes.workstation: Certified and supported for professional software, but limited to pro GPUs, not gaming ones. Fine for modeling, short on power for serious visualization. Most architects don't need the certification, so don't pay the premium for it unless your firm requires it.
PrebuiltTypeNotes.gaming: The best value when you need a powerful GPU. The cooling and power supply it needs come standard, so it beats a pricier workstation at Enscape, Lumion, and V-Ray.

Laptops.name: HP ZBook Ultra G1a
Laptops.note: Ryzen AI Max+ 395, 128 GB unified, 14-inch OLED. The integrated Radeon stands in for a discrete GPU, strong for modeling. The 128 GB holds large visualization scenes, but the integrated GPU is too slow to render them. Battery is the weak point.

Laptops.name: Lenovo ThinkPad P1 Gen 8
Laptops.note: Arrow Lake, RTX PRO 2000 (8 GB), up to 64 GB, 3.2K tandem OLED. A true workstation at this weight, with the best keyboard here.

Laptops.name: Asus ProArt P16
Laptops.note: Ryzen AI 9 HX 370, RTX 5070, up to 64 GB, 16-inch 4K OLED. A polished creator laptop. Memory is soldered, so configure it up front.

Laptops.name: Asus ROG Zephyrus G16
Laptops.note: Core Ultra 9, up to RTX 5090, 16-inch 2.5K OLED. Lighter than a workstation with an excellent screen, though the Intel model runs warm under load.

Laptops.name: Asus ROG Zephyrus G14
Laptops.note: Ryzen AI 9, up to RTX 5080, 14-inch 3K OLED. Memory is soldered, so configure it up front. The thin 14-inch chassis runs the GPU at lower wattage, so it trails heavier machines.

Laptops.name: Razer Blade 16
Laptops.note: Ryzen AI 9 HX 370, up to RTX 5090, 16-inch OLED. The thinnest way to carry a 5090. Premium build, but Razer's support is inconsistent.

Laptops.name: Lenovo Legion Pro 7i
Laptops.note: Core Ultra 9 275HX, up to RTX 5090, 16-inch OLED. Gaming-desktop power for the price. Loud, and desk-bound.

Laptops.name: Lenovo ThinkPad P16 Gen 3
Laptops.note: Core Ultra 9 285HX, RTX PRO 5000 (24 GB), up to 192 GB ECC. A flagship mobile workstation, certified for pro apps.

Laptops.name: HP ZBook Fury 16 G1i
Laptops.note: Core Ultra 9 285HX, RTX PRO 5000 (24 GB), up to 192 GB. A 280W adapter and three-fan vapor chamber give it the best sustained-rendering thermals here.

Laptops.name: Dell Pro Max 16 Plus
Laptops.note: Core Ultra 9 285HX, RTX PRO 5000 (24 GB ECC), 128 GB, 4K OLED. Replaceable GPU and memory make it the serviceable pick. AEC Magazine rates it highly.

Laptops.name: Lenovo ThinkPad X1 Carbon Gen 13
Laptops.note: Core Ultra 7 (Lunar Lake), 32 GB, 14-inch. The standard ultraportable. All-day battery, no discrete GPU, for documents and drafting.

Laptops.name: Lenovo ThinkPad X9 14 Aura Edition
Laptops.note: Core Ultra 7 (Lunar Lake), 32 GB, 14-inch 2.8K OLED. A premium ultraportable for documents and drafting. A nicer screen and build than the X1 Carbon, with no more power.

Laptops.name: Asus TUF Gaming A16
Laptops.note: Ryzen 7, RTX 5060 (8 GB), upgradeable to 64 GB, 16-inch. Durable to MIL-STD and affordable, with long battery life for a gaming laptop.

Laptops.name: Lenovo LOQ 16
Laptops.note: Intel or Ryzen with an RTX 5050/5060, up to 32 GB across two slots. The budget pick. Configurable, and easy to upgrade later.

Laptops.name: Acer Predator Helios Neo 16
Laptops.note: Core Ultra 9 275HX, up to RTX 5070 Ti, 16-inch 2.5K OLED. A high-wattage GPU for studios that need real-time visualization without a workstation price.

Laptops.name: MacBook Air 15" M5
Laptops.note: M5, fanless, up to 32 GB unified, 15-inch. All-day battery for documents and light drafting, though the fanless design slows it under sustained load.

Laptops.name: MacBook Pro 14" M5 Pro
Laptops.note: M5 Pro, up to 64 GB unified, 14-inch XDR. The everyday Mac for ArchiCAD, Rhino, and SketchUp.

Laptops.name: MacBook Pro 16" M5 Pro
Laptops.note: M5 Pro, up to 64 GB unified, 16-inch XDR. More screen and sustained power than the 14-inch. The one-machine Mac.

Laptops.name: MacBook Pro 16" M5 Max
Laptops.note: M5 Max, 64–128 GB unified, 16-inch XDR. Serious GPU cores for Enscape and V-Ray on Metal.

Laptops.name: MacBook Air 13" M5
Laptops.note: M5, fanless, up to 32 GB unified, 13-inch. The budget Mac. Small screen, so dock it to a monitor, and it slows under sustained load.

Laptops.name: MacBook Pro 14" M5
Laptops.note: Base M5 with a fan, 14-inch XDR. Better sustained performance than the Air, for modeling on the move.

VRAM.def: A dedicated GPU's own memory. It holds the scene while you work, so it sets how large a scene fits.

unified memory.def: On Apple Silicon, one pool of memory shared by the processor and the graphics. It counts as both RAM and VRAM.

single-core.def: How fast one CPU core runs. Modeling and drafting depend on this, since they work one operation at a time.

CPU core.def: One of the independent processing units in a CPU. Final rendering uses all of them at once; modeling depends on the speed of just one.

GPU core.def: The graphics units on an Apple Silicon chip. More of them speed up real-time visualization.

integrated graphics.def: The graphics built into the CPU. Fine for documents and 2D drafting, unreliable for 3D viewports.

dedicated GPU.def: A separate graphics card, not the one built into the CPU. Modeling and visualization both need one.

3D V-Cache.def: Extra fast memory AMD stacks onto the processor. It speeds up Revit and other modeling work.

X3D.def: AMD's chips that carry 3D V-Cache. The fastest processors for Revit.

Rosetta.def: Apple's built-in translator that runs Intel Mac apps on Apple Silicon, at a small speed cost.

Metal.def: Apple's graphics framework, its counterpart to DirectX. Mac renderers like V-Ray work through it.

regeneration.def: Revit or CAD recomputing the model after a change. A faster CPU core shortens the wait.

hybrid rendering.def: Final rendering that uses the GPU and the CPU together, which finishes faster than the CPU alone.

Threadripper.def: AMD's very-high-core-count processors, built for a dedicated render machine.

xref.def: A drawing referenced inside another in AutoCAD, so shared sheets and details update everywhere at once.
